Subject: Accelerator cohort — question on edu/nonprofit pricing and baseline minimums

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for making time to chat last week. LearnLaunch runs a student-focused accelerator (nonprofit) that serves ~100 teams per year — many are student founders or university-affiliated projects. A bunch of the startups want to integrate Redwood-hosted APIs for chat and retrieval. Before we set up demos, can you confirm: 1) whether LearnLaunch (as a nonprofit accelerator) is eligible for the education/nonprofit rate; and 2) if not, whether we can get an exception to the base monthly commitment for cohort programs?

Rough usage profile for the upcoming cohort (June–Aug): aggregate ~1.5–2M tokens/month across ~25 pilot teams, mostly bursts during office hours. We don’t yet have EIN paperwork for each team — some are student projects, some are early-stage LLCs.

Attached: accelerator_overview.pdf (program background) and cohort_list.csv (anonymized list of participating teams + school affiliation).

Primary asks: quick confirmation on eligibility, high-level rate card for hosted API (tokens/embeddings), and whether Redwood would consider a short-term pilot exception (90 days) with lower minimums or credits. If you prefer, we can provide proof of nonprofit status and a letter from our education partner.

Appreciate a straight answer — we need this for orientation materials.

Best,
Sarah Patel
Director, LearnLaunch Accelerator
Sarah.Patel@learnlaunch.org

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear summary and for the attachments. Short answers up front: LearnLaunch is the right kind of program for our education/nonprofit consideration, but eligibility depends on the legal status of the program or the sponsoring institution (we can qualify the accelerator itself or individual teams in some cases). We do offer two practical paths for accelerator cohorts:

- Education/Nonprofit program: requires proof (501(c)(3) or university affiliation) and typically grants a tiered discount on hosted API calls/embeddings. This is intended for programs run by a recognized nonprofit/academic partner.
- Accelerator pilot package: a time-limited credit + pilot-rate exception for cohorts without full nonprofit paperwork (case-by-case approval).

Given your projected volume (1.5–2M tokens/month), the fastest route for onboarding is an accelerator pilot: we can grant credits to cover initial usage and a temporary rate adjustment for the first 60–90 days while you collect paperwork for longer-term eligibility. To evaluate an exception I need: 1) confirmation the program itself is nonprofit or university-affiliated (if available), 2) a scoped list of participating teams (you included cohort_list.csv which helps), and 3) a short note about expected peak token bursts (how many requests/session typical).

I’ve looped in Marissa (Enterprise Sales Lead) to review the commercial exception. I’ll follow up internally and get back with a concrete pilot proposal (credits + pilot rate) by EOD tomorrow.

If you’re comfortable, please reply with the best contact for legal/partnership paperwork and whether LearnLaunch prefers a single master MOU with Redwood or team-level attestations.

Cheers,
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Internal: LearnLaunch accelerator — request for pilot-rate exception (details + recommendation)

Marissa / Aditya — FYI: LearnLaunch (nonprofit accelerator) asked about eligibility for edu/nonprofit pricing and a short-term exception to the hosted API baseline minimum. Summary: 25 pilot teams, est. 1.5–2M tokens/month aggregate, need 90-day runway to collect paperwork from individual teams/university partners. Attachments: accelerator_overview.pdf, cohort_list.csv.

Commercial ask from customer: waive the standard monthly minimum for a cohort pilot OR provide sufficient credits/discounts so teams can evaluate without the full commit.

Recommendation (to close quickly and de-risk):
- Offer a pilot package: $5,000 in platform credits applied to the hosted API, valid for 90 days, plus a temporary pilot token rate of $0.0008/token (hosted generation) for up to 2M tokens/month during the 90 days. After 90 days revert to standard rate card (or convert to EDU/Nonprofit tier if paperwork provided).
- Require a short MOU signed by LearnLaunch and a single point of contact; require either: program-level nonprofit proof (EIN + charters) OR university sponsorship note.

Rationale: $5k credits covers lightweight experimentation and demos; pilot-rate reduces immediate cost friction but ties to a defined timebox (limits revenue risk). Expected impact: small revenue deferral but higher chance of multi-team adoption and future Dedicated/Dedicated Reserved deals.

Questions for you: 1) OK to approve $5k credits + pilot rate as exception? 2) Any objections to the $0.0008/token pilot rate (we currently have standard hosted generation at ~$0.0012/token for comparable profile)? 3) Do we want legal to prepare a one-page MOU template?

If approved, I’ll send the external confirmation and DocuSign link.

Thanks,
Priyom
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.example>

Hi Sarah — good news: we can run the pilot for LearnLaunch. Summary of what we can offer for the June–Aug cohort: 

1) Pilot credits: $5,000 Redwood platform credits, valid for 90 days from activation (applied at account level).
2) Temporary pilot rate: $0.0008 per generation token (hosted API) for up to 2M tokens/month for the 90-day pilot window. Overages beyond 2M tokens/month will bill at the standard hosted rate.
3) Eligibility for a longer-term Education/Nonprofit tier after the pilot if LearnLaunch provides program-level nonprofit proof (EIN/charter) or sponsorship confirmation from a university partner.

Requirements / next steps:
- Please confirm you accept the pilot package.
- We’ll need a signed one-page MOU (I’ll send a DocuSign link once you confirm).
- If you want team-level subsidies after the pilot we’ll need the paperwork for those teams (we can advise on minimal attestations).

I’ve cc’d Marissa on this thread. If you’re good, I’ll open HubSpot deal RWD-PA-2026-045 and send the MOU/DocuSign.

Thanks again — looking forward to getting your cohort onboarded.

Best,
